## What was observed

During a Tests-tab greening session (su-7c7f465d, 2026-06-24), 5 Claude Code
Task-tool subagents were spawned in parallel to fix integration-test clusters.
The **parent session authenticated and ran fine**. All 5 spawned subagents
**died after 12-39 tool calls** with:

```
API Error: 401 Invalid authentication credentials
Not logged in · Please run /login
```

Each subagent had made partial, unverified edits before dying. Net effect at
the time: parallel Task-tool fan-out from an su session was unusable, forcing
serial work. Filed as EI-3294.

## What this is NOT

Two related-but-distinct classes of subagent failure are already understood
and are **not** this bug — don't conflate them if you're re-investigating:

- **429 "Server is temporarily limiting requests"** (a transient per-client
  burst throttle from launching 2+ heavy subagents in parallel) — a *rate*
  error, dies after 0-7 tool calls, fixed by launching subagents solo/sequential.
  See the su playbook / mem0 recall for this class.
- **The Max-OAuth opus 429-shunt** fixed by always prepending the exact
  `CLAUDE_CODE_IDENTIFIER` system block (`chat-stream.ts buildSystemParam()`) —
  applies to papercusp's own in-process anthropic-direct calls (scout/gym/etc),
  not the CLI's built-in Task tool.

EI-3294 is a **401 auth failure**, not a 429 rate-limit, and it took
12-39 tool calls (real elapsed time) to manifest, not an immediate burst.

## Working hypothesis (UNCONFIRMED — no live repro access)

As of this writing subagents are **denied by default fleet-wide** (owner
mandate 2026-07-02, `no-subagent-deny.ts`) for an unrelated reason
(uncontrolled fan-out outside the orchestrator's spawn graph), which means a
default psu session can no longer hit this at all — so a live repro requires
deliberately re-enabling `--allow-subagents`, which a fleet member session
does not have. The hypothesis below was built from static analysis
(`spawn-env.ts`, `resolveAccountPin` in `bootstrap-su.ts`), not a fresh repro,
and should be verified live before being treated as proven:

- On the **default account route** (no `--account` flag / `--account default`,
  the psu default), a claude session authenticates with the **local OAuth
  login** (`~/.claude` credentials), which the CLI itself manages, including
  **token refresh/rotation** — entirely inside the closed-source client, not
  observable or controllable from papercusp's spawn code.
- A Task/Agent subagent that runs long enough (12-39 tool calls, i.e. real
  wall-clock minutes) could plausibly cross the local token's refresh window.
  If the CLI's refresh **rotates** the token (invalidating the old one) and
  the subagent's own auth state doesn't observe the parent's refresh (or
  races it), the subagent would start failing with exactly this 401 while
  the parent — which owns the refresh — keeps working. This is consistent
  with the observed "dies after N calls, parent fine" shape, but has not
  been confirmed against actual CLI internals or logs.
- On the **gateway-routed** account route (`--account auto` or a pinned pool
  account), the CLI instead holds a **static, non-expiring**
  `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` placeholder (`GATEWAY_CLIENT_AUTH_TOKEN` in
  `spawn-env.ts`) — the real OAuth is held and refreshed server-side by the
  localhost gateway (`:8788`), transparently, per request. A client-side
  local-token-refresh race of the kind hypothesized above **cannot occur**
  under this route, because the client never sees a real, expiring token at
  all. This is the basis for the mitigation below — it is inference from the
  mechanism, not a confirmed fix (no A/B repro was run).

## What's actually landed (a warning, not a fix)

There is no papercusp code responsible for the CLI's internal Task/Agent
subagent credential handling — it is inside the closed-source `claude`
binary, outside this repo's reach. What *did* land
(`apps/operator/scripts/psu-launcher.mjs` `subagentGatewayRiskNotice`,
2026-07-20): a **non-fatal, print-once warning** at su/role launch time when
`--allow-subagents` is combined with the default (non-gateway) account route
— i.e. exactly the untested, at-risk combination — pointing at this doc and
suggesting gateway routing as a way to sidestep the hypothesized race. It
does **not** auto-switch the account route: per the su playbook, account
routing is the owner's call, never silently changed by an agent.

## If you're revisiting this

1. **Get a live repro** with `--allow-subagents` explicitly granted (owner
   ask, or a session with that authority) — instrument the subagent's exact
   token/credential state at the moment of the 401, not just the symptom.
2. **A/B the account route**: run the same subagent fan-out on `--account
   default` vs `--account auto` — if the gateway route survives where default
   fails, that confirms the hypothesis and the warning above can graduate to
   a stronger guard (or the default could be reconsidered for
   `--allow-subagents` launches specifically — an owner decision, not
   something to change silently).
3. If disproven, remove `subagentGatewayRiskNotice` and its call sites (2
   in `psu-launcher.mjs`) and this doc — don't leave a debunked warning live.
